comment: CHAOS-4632 hand-labelled question set — the GATING MEASUREMENT's ground truth.
The design's §9-S2 gate is LABELLED SEMANTIC CORRECTNESS, not emission rate, and it MUST include
NEGATIVE cases: 'a model reliably emitting GroupKind=project for Q-A scores 100% on emission and
builds the wrong group axis'. Precedence row 1 fires on GroupKind ALONE, so a model spuriously
emitting it on a plain single-subject status question routes that question to a grouped cohort.
The number that matters is therefore FALSE EMISSION as much as correct emission.
HOW TO READ A ROW. expect_group_kind / expect_scope_anchor / expect_scope_anchor_kind /
expect_requested_kind are the CORRECT values for that question. An EMPTY string means the field
MUST be absent — those rows are the negative cases, and they are the majority of this set on
purpose. expect_family is what the §4.2 precedence table should produce GIVEN correct signals.
expect_scope_anchor is compared case-insensitively after trimming, because it is a retrieval
pointer rather than a value — the graph resolves it, nothing branches on its text. Where more
than one verbatim substring names the SAME anchor, expect_scope_anchor_any lists the accepted
forms and expect_scope_anchor holds the canonical one; scoring accepts any member. Demanding one
exact string would measure the model's choice of substring rather than whether it found the
right anchor, which is not what the anchor is for.
THIS FILE IS GROUND TRUTH, NOT OUTPUT. It is authored by hand and reviewed as a claim about what
these questions MEAN. Never regenerate it from model output: a label set derived from the thing it

cases.question: What are the project statuses for each team, and what are the main drivers?
cases.note: Acceptance question Q-A. 'for each team' is the grouping phrase; the groups ARE teams.

cases.question: What's are the project statuses for each team, and what are the main drivers?
cases.note: Q-A as chris actually typed it. The typo must not change the interpretation; this pair is the typo-robustness probe.

cases.question: What are the statuses of the fullchaos team's projects?
cases.note: Acceptance question Q-B. The named term is the SCOPE, not the subject — this is the asymmetry row 2 exists for, and the CHAOS-4622 §2 defect is being asked to pick ONE subject here.

cases.question: What is the status of the Dev Health Ops project?
cases.note: BAR question Q1. NEGATIVE for all three signals. This is the discriminating control: a model that emits group_kind here routes a plain status question to a grouped cohort.

cases.question: Which teams are struggling, and why?
cases.note: BAR question Q2. NEGATIVE for group_kind: a discovered cohort is a FLAT ranked list, not a partition. 'teams' is what is being ranked, not what the results are grouped BY — this is the single most likely false-emission trap in the set.

cases.question: Why is the acr project struggling?
cases.note: NEGATIVE. A why-phrased single-subject question. Merged into subject_investigation by decision D1; drivers are ATTEMPTED, never required.

cases.question: How many teams own the dev-health-acr repository?
cases.note: SCOPED, and it took two review rounds to get here — the history is the point. Revision 1 labelled requested_kind=repository (wrong: the answer is a count of TEAMS; the repository bounds the count). Revision 2 fixed that but kept family=subject_investigation with an EMPTY anchor. Main's human review caught the remaining inconsistency, and it is correct: this question is the structural MIRROR of pos-scoped-repositories. There, a named team bounds a cohort of repositories; here, a named repository bounds a cohort of teams. Same asymmetry, opposite direction. 'How many' is PRESENTATION of that cohort — a render concern, not a family: you cannot count the teams without resolving the cohort of teams. Labelling it subject_investigation with no anchor would have taught exactly the surface-form rule cases 8 and 9 exist to defeat, in reverse: 'aggregate questions have no anchor'. NEGATIVE only for group_kind, which stays empty: a bounded cohort is not a partitioned one.

cases.question: What is the fullchaos team's status?
cases.note: NEGATIVE for the anchor, and the sharpest negative in the set: it has the possessive SURFACE FORM of Q-B but no asymmetry — the answer is about the team ITSELF. A model keying on "X's Y" grammar rather than on meaning emits an anchor here and gets it wrong.

cases.question: Which repositories does the platform team own?
cases.note: POSITIVE for the anchor without the possessive form — the asymmetry is real (repositories scoped by a team) but the grammar differs from Q-B. Pairs with neg-possessive-but-same-kind: together they check the model reads MEANING, not surface form, in both directions. expect_scope_anchor_any exists because the live run emitted 'platform' on one replicate and 'platform team' on the other, and scoring that as an error was MY label being too strict: the design is explicit that ScopeAnchorTerm is a RETRIEVAL POINTER, not a value — nothing branches on its text, only on whether it resolved, and both strings are verbatim substrings naming the same team. A scorer that demanded one exact string would be measuring the model's choice of substring rather than whether it identified the right anchor.

cases.question: Show me open incidents per repository.
cases.note: POSITIVE for group_kind via 'per X' rather than 'for each X', and with a grouping kind that is NOT team — so a model that has simply learned 'group_kind is always team' fails this row while passing qa-grouped-clean.

cases.question: Compare the acr project to the ask-dev project over the last 90 days.
cases.note: NEGATIVE for both new signals. Two named subjects, no grouping, no scope. Row 3 territory.

cases.question: What should I worry about?
cases.note: NEGATIVE for everything. An open question with no subject axis at all. A model emitting any of the three signals here is inventing structure from nothing, which is the failure mode with the least excuse.
